### Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results


10/28/2026


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE: FBRT) (“FBRT” or the “Company”) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


During the third quarter, FBRT increased fully converted book value(1) per share and continued to execute on its key priorities, including accretive share repurchases, resolving legacy assets and growing the contribution from its Agency Business.


**Third Quarter 2026 Summary**


- GAAP net loss of $(27.0) million or $(0.41) per diluted common share
- Distributable Earnings (a non-GAAP financial measure) of $3.3 million, or $(0.02) per diluted common share on a fully converted basis (1)
- Distributable Earnings before realized losses (a non-GAAP financial measure) of $25.8 million, or $0.24 per diluted common share on a fully converted basis (1)
- Repurchased 7,433,748 shares of common stock at an average price of $8.14 per share for an aggregate of $60.5 million, resulting in $0.55 per diluted common share of book value accretion on a fully converted basis (1)
- Book value of $14.26 per diluted common share on a fully converted basis (1), an increase of $0.02 from the prior quarter
- Adjusted (2) fully converted (1) book value per share of $15.13, an increase of $0.39 from the prior quarter
- Core portfolio:


- Principal balance of $4.1 billion across 175 loans, with an average loan size of $23.2 million, and 83% collateralized by multifamily properties
- Closed $249.3 million of new loan commitments and funded $284.8 million on new and existing loans
- Received loan repayments of $405.5 million
- Average portfolio risk rating of 2.4, unchanged from prior quarter


- Agency Business segment:


- Servicing portfolio grew by $1.4 billion to $61.3 billion (3)
- Originated $670.4 million of new loan commitments under programs with Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and HUD
- Mortgage Servicing Rights ("MSRs") book value at $201.2 million, with another $8.1 million in MSR book value related to loan commitments and funded agency loans


- Declared a third quarter common stock cash dividend of $0.20, representing an annualized 5.6% yield on fully converted book value (1), or 12.8% yield on current trading price (4)
- Total liquidity of $407.2 million, including $100.8 million of cash and cash equivalents


**Portfolio and Investment Activity**


*Core portfolio* : For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company closed $249.3 million of new loan commitments, funded $284.8 million of principal balance on new and existing loans, and received loan repayments of $405.5 million. FBRT's average portfolio risk rating was 2.4, unchanged from the prior quarter. At quarter end, the Company had 13 loans with a principal balance of $333.6 million on its watch list, six of which are risk rated a four and seven of which are risk rated a five.


*Conduit:* For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company originated $61.5 million of fixed rate conduit loans and sold $54.5 million of conduit loans for a gain of $1.0 million, gross of related derivatives.


*Agency Business segment:* For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company originated $670.4 million of new commitments under programs with Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and HUD and managed a servicing portfolio of $61.3 billion.


*Real estate owned and equity method investments:* For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company had ten foreclosure real estate owned positions totaling $339.5 million, one investment real estate owned position of $113.9 million, and six equity method investment positions of $88.7 million.


*Allowance for credit losses* : During the quarter, the Company recognized a net provision for credit losses of $43.1 million. Provision for our core portfolio was $37.7 million, comprised of a specific allowance provision of $38.7 million, partially offset by a general benefit of $1.0 million. Provision for our Agency Business was $5.4 million, comprised of a general provision of $5.0 million and a provision for specific allowance of $0.4 million.


**Book Value**


As of September 30, 2026, book value was $14.26 per diluted common share on a fully converted basis(1).


**Share Repurchase Program**


During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 7,433,748 shares of common stock at an average price of $8.14 per share for an aggregate of $60.5 million, which represents a $0.55 per share increase to book value on a fully converted basis(1). On October 27, 2026, the Company’s board of directors extended the program to December 31, 2027.


**Subsequent Events**


On October 15, 2026, the Company called all of the outstanding notes issued by BSPRT 2023-FL10 Issuer, Ltd., a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of the Company. The notes had an outstanding principal balance of $267.2 million at the time of redemption.


**Distributable Earnings and Distributable Earnings to Common**


Distributable Earnings is a non-GAAP measure, which the Company defines as GAAP net income (loss), adjusted for (i) non-cash CLO amortization acceleration and amortization over the expected useful life of the Company's CLOs, (ii) unrealized gains and losses on loans and derivatives, including CECL reserves and impairments, net of realized gains and losses, as described further below, (iii) non-cash equity compensation expense, (iv) depreciation and amortization, (v) subordinated performance fee accruals/(reversal), (vi) realized gains and losses on debt extinguishment and CLO calls, (vii) non-cash income from mortgage servicing rights, and (viii) certain other non-cash items. Distributable Earnings before realized losses, a non-GAAP measure, presents Distributable Earnings gross of realized gain (loss) on debt extinguishment and realized gain (loss) on loans and real estate owned. Further, Distributable Earnings to Common, a non-GAAP measure, presents Distributable Earnings net of (x) perpetual preferred stock dividend payments and (y) non-controlling interests in joint ventures.


As noted above, we exclude unrealized gains and losses on loans and other investments, including CECL reserves and impairments, from our calculation of Distributable Earnings and include realized gains and losses. The nature of these adjustments is described more fully in the footnotes to our reconciliation tables. GAAP loan loss reserves and any property impairment losses have been excluded from Distributable Earnings consistent with other unrealized losses pursuant to our existing definition of Distributable Earnings. We expect to only recognize such potential credit or property impairment losses in Distributable Earnings if and when such amounts are deemed nonrecoverable upon a realization event. This is generally at the time a loan is repaid, or in the case of a foreclosure or other property, when the underlying asset is sold. Amounts may also be deemed non-recoverable if, in our determination, it is nearly certain the carrying amounts will not be collected or realized. The realized loss amount reflected in Distributable Earnings will generally equal the difference between the cash received and the Distributable Earnings basis of the asset. The timing of any such loss realization in our Distributable Earnings may differ materially from the timing of the corresponding loss reserves, charge-offs or impairments in our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP.


The Company believes that Distributable Earnings, Distributable Earnings before realized losses and Distributable Earnings to Common provide meaningful information to consider in addition to the disclosed GAAP results. The Company believes Distributable Earnings, Distributable Earnings before realized losses and Distributable Earnings to Common are useful financial metrics for existing and potential future holders of its common stock as historically, over time, Distributable Earnings to Common has been an indicator of common dividends per share. As a REIT, the Company generally must distribute annually at least 90% of its taxable income, subject to certain adjustments, and therefore believes dividends are one of the principal reasons stockholders may invest in its common stock. Further, Distributable Earnings to Common helps investors evaluate performance excluding the effects of certain transactions and GAAP adjustments that the Company does not believe are necessarily indicative of current loan portfolio performance and the Company's operations and is one of the performance metrics the Company's board of directors considers when dividends are declared.


Distributable Earnings, Distributable Earnings before realized losses and Distributable Earnings to Common do not represent net income (loss) and should not be considered as an alternative to GAAP net income (loss). The methodology for calculating Distributable Earnings, Distributable Earnings before realized losses and Distributable Earnings to Common may differ from the methodologies employed by other companies and thus may not be comparable to the Distributable Earnings reported by other companies.


Please refer to the financial statements and reconciliation of GAAP Net Income to Distributable Earnings, Distributable Earnings before Realized Losses and Distributable Earnings to Common included at the end of this release for further information.

**About Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc.**


Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE: FBRT) is a real estate investment trust that originates, acquires and manages a diversified portfolio of commercial real estate debt secured by properties located in the United States. As of September 30, 2026, FBRT had approximately $6.0 billion of assets. FBRT is externally managed by Benefit Street Partners L.L.C., a wholly owned subsidiary of Franklin Templeton, Inc. For further information, please visit[www.fbrtreit.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.fbrtreit.com&esheet=54630662&newsitemid=20261028917636&lan=en-US&anchor=www.fbrtreit.com&index=4&md5=a5a66c9ca6a2d1d3a9a87e4be003b00c) .


**About Benefit Street Partners**


Benefit Street Partners is an alternative credit pioneer with $96 billion in assets under management as of August 31, 2026 (including Apera). It seeks to deliver attractive, risk-adjusted returns through its deep specialism, long-term relationships and global reach. A wholly owned subsidiary of Franklin Templeton, BSP is focused on credit. Through its disciplined, solutions-oriented approach, BSP unlocks opportunities across market cycles and geographies. The firm manages strategies spanning private debt, real estate debt, structured credit, and liquid loans. For more information, visit[www.bspcredit.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.bspcredit.com&esheet=54630662&newsitemid=20261028917636&lan=en-US&anchor=www.bspcredit.com&index=5&md5=eee79f2a65ea2e54b84e19d6ccbf9706) .


**About Franklin Templeton**


Franklin Templeton is a trusted investment partner, delivering tailored solutions that align with clients’ strategic goals. With deep portfolio management expertise across public and private markets, we combine investment excellence with cutting-edge technology. Since our founding in 1947, we have empowered clients through strategic partnership, forward-looking insights, and continuous innovation – providing the tools and resources to navigate change and capture opportunity.


With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under management as of September 30, 2026, Franklin Templeton operates globally in more than 35 countries.


To learn more, visit[www.franklintempleton.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.franklintempleton.com&esheet=54630662&newsitemid=20261028917636&lan=en-US&anchor=www.franklintempleton.com&index=6&md5=bca565f861602a0df1175b03d9ba3116) and follow us on[LinkedIn](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fcompany%2Ffranklin-templeton%2F&esheet=54630662&newsitemid=20261028917636&lan=en-US&anchor=LinkedIn&index=7&md5=d3df00ce6e826494dc1bcf9086c3ba47) .
